subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a new global bootstrap-context knob after the legacy hook compatibility issue is fixed?
rationale: The PR adds a new user-facing config/default surface that changes agent session context policy; repository policy treats config/default additions and session-state behavior as maintainer/product decisions, even when the implementation is otherwise repairable.

options.title: Accept after compatibility repair
options.body: Keep the new tier concept, but require the no-override path to preserve existing `bootstrap-extra-files` behavior and review the refreshed PR before merge.

options.title: Defer core config surface
options.body: Close or park the PR and continue using existing hook/context-size controls until maintainers want a broader bootstrap-context policy design.

options.title: Narrow to hook-only behavior
options.body: Drop the global default knob and keep only a smaller hook filtering improvement if maintainers want less new config surface.

recommendation.title: Accept after compatibility repair
recommendation.body: Keep the new tier concept, but require the no-override path to preserve existing `bootstrap-extra-files` behavior and review the refreshed PR before merge.
